translations.@message_module_state_faulted: This module is in a faulted state: something it installed could not be removed. Check the Automatics log for details, then change this setting again to retry.
translations.@message_module_runtime_toggle_degraded: This Harmony build cannot remove patches at runtime. Turning this module off only gates it, and its patches stay applied until the game is restarted.
translations.@config_system_enable_logging_descriptio: Specify whether to enable log output. System initialization logs for Automatics are always output regardless of the value of this option.
translations.@config_system_log_level_to_allow_loggin: Specify the log level that allows logging.
translations.@config_general_custom_animal_descriptio:
Any animal can be added.
Identifier: A unique string that does not overlap with any other identifier. Whitespace is not allowed.
Label: The name of the animal. Mainly used in the GUI. If you specify an internal name, it will be translated automatically.
Pattern: A pattern matching the internal name of the animal. Exact matches are evaluated. Prefix the pattern with r/ to use a regular expression.

Label: The name of the dungeon. Mainly used in the GUI. If you specify an internal name, it will be translated automatically.
Pattern: A pattern matching the prefab name of the dungeon. Exact matches are evaluated. Prefix the pattern with r/ to use a regular expression.

translations.@config_automatic_door_enable_automatic_: Specify whether to enable the feature that automatically opens and closes the door.
translations.@config_automatic_door_allow_automatic_d: Specify which doors are allowed to open and close automatically.
translations.@config_automatic_door_interval_to_open_: Specify the interval at which the process of automatically opening the door is called. If set to less than 0.1, the function to automatically open the door will be disabled. (Unit: second)
translations.@config_automatic_door_interval_to_close: Specify the interval at which the process of automatically closing the door is called. If set to less than 0.1, the function to automatically close the door will be disabled. (Unit: second)
translations.@config_automatic_door_distance_for_auto: Specify how close the player must be to the door in order for it to open automatically. (Unit: meter)

Specify how far the player must be from the door for the door to close automatically. While automatic opening is active, a value smaller than Distance For Automatic Opening is replaced by that distance. (Unit: meter)
translations.@config_automatic_door_automatic_door_en: Specify a shortcut key to enable/disable the automatic door.
Specify where a message is displayed when the automatic door is enabled or disabled by a shortcut key.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_enable_automat: Specify whether to enable the feature that automatically pins objects and locations to the map.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_dynamic_object: Specify the range of dynamic objects to be explored. "Dynamic objects" are objects that change position, such as animals and monsters. Set to 0 to disable pinning of dynamic objects. (Unit: meter)
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_static_object_: Specify the range of static objects to be explored. "Static objects" are objects that do not change their position, such as flora and minerals. Setting this to 0 disables pinning of static objects, including portals and locations. (Unit: meter)
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_location_mappi: Specify the range of locations to be explored. A "location" is a specific place, such as a dungeon or a fuling village. Setting this to 0 disables location pinning. (Unit: meter)
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_hide_unexplore: Hide Automatic Mapping pins whose position is outside the explored map. Saved pins are hidden, not deleted.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_allow_pinning_: Allow Pinning Animal
Specify the animals to pin automatically.
Allow Pinning Monster
Specify the monsters to pin automatically.
Allow Pinning Flora
Specify the flora to pin automatically.
Allow Pinning Mineral
Specify the minerals to pin automatically.
Allow Pinning Spawner
Specify the spawners to pin automatically.
Allow Pinning Vehicle
Specify the vehicles to pin automatically.
Allow Pinning Other Object
Specify the other objects to pin automatically.
Allow Pinning Dungeon
Specify the dungeons to pin automatically.
Allow Pinning Spot
Specify the spots to pin automatically.
Allow Pinning Portal
Enable automatic pinning of portals. Portals are treated as static objects.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_not_pinning_ta: Exclude tamed animals from automatic pinning.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_static_object_: Specify the interval at which static objects are mapped. Setting to 0 disables periodic static object mapping. (Unit: second)
Specify the interval at which static objects will be cached. Mapping of static objects uses this cache. (Unit: second)
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_save_static_ob: Specify whether to save the pins of static objects.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_remove_pins_of: Specify whether or not to automatically remove pins of objects that have been destroyed and no longer exist.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_flora_pins_mer: When pinning flora, it recursively searches for the same flora that exist within a specified range and merges them into a single pin. (Unit: meter)
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_need_to_equip_: Need To Equip Wishbone For Underground Minerals
Specify whether the wishbone needs to be equipped to pin underground minerals.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_static_object_: Specify shortcut keys for mapping static objects. Setting this item disables the static object mapping at regular intervals, so that it is performed only once each time the shortcut key is pressed.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_pin_object_key: Press this shortcut to save a map pin for what you are looking at, using its display name and icon-pack icon. Looking at a world-generated location (its structure, the ground within its area or a dungeon's interior) pins the location with the name and icon Automatic Mapping recognizes. Player-built pieces, creatures, trees, deposits and other objects keep their own pins, and other bare ground gets an unnamed pin. Unbound by default; requires the module to be running.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_pin_object_ran: Maximum distance in meters from the camera for pinning the object you are looking at.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_navigation_sta: Specify the modifier key used to start navigation by left-clicking a pin on the large map. Left click is fixed.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_enable_navigat: Specify whether a swarm of small glowing lights leads you toward the navigation target. It follows the ground in a straight line, stops spawning within 5 m of the target and is hidden while the large map is open.
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_navigation_gui: Specify the HTML color code of the navigation guide swarm. Examples: #C6F27A, #C6F27AFF
translations.@config_automatic_mapping_mapping_perfor: Specify whether to measure automatic mapping performance and write the metrics to the BepInEx log at the Info level. The metrics are written only when Logging is enabled and Log Level To Allow Logging includes Info.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_enable_auto: Specify whether to enable the ability to automatically perform tasks such as cooking, refining, and refueling.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_storage_con: Specify the HTML color code used for the storage connection effect shown by automatic processing. Examples: #4FA9FF, #4FA9FFFF
translations.@config_automatic_processing_allow_conta: Specify containers that allow automatic operations such as item supply and storage.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_refuel_fire: Specify the fires and lights that are refuelled from nearby containers. They share the settings whose names start with "Fires and lights:".
translations.@config_automatic_processing_allow_proce: Specify the automatic processes to allow for $1. "Craft" produces items by automatically consuming the required materials. "Refuel" automatically supplies fuel items. "Store" automatically stores the produced items in containers. "Charge" automatically replenishes consumable items such as ammo.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_container_s: Specify the maximum distance $1 will search for containers. (Unit: meters)
translations.@config_automatic_processing_container_r: Specify the maximum number of nearby containers that $1 will reference in distance order. Set to 0 for unlimited. The default is 0.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_material_co: $1: Number Of Materials To Stop Supplying

When the number of material items stored in the container is about to become less than the specified quantity, the supply of materials to $1 will be stopped. If set to 0, stopping the material supply based on the number of material items will be disabled.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_supply_only: $1: Supply Only If Materials Run Out
Supply one material item only when the materials supplied to $1 run out.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_fuel_count_: $1: Number Of Fuels To Stop Refuel

When the number of fuel items stored in the container is about to become less than the specified quantity, refuel to $1 will be stopped. If set to 0, stopping refuel based on the number of fuel items will be disabled.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_product_sta: $1: Number Of Product Stacks To Stop Processing

Stops $1 once the containers it uses hold this many stacks of its product in total; a station that crafts also counts what it is still making. A station that crafts stops taking materials; a station that only stores its product stops moving it into containers. If set to 0, there is no limit.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_refuel_only: Refuel only when material items are supplied to $1.
$1: Refuel Only If Fuels Run Out
Refuel only when the fuel for $1 runs out.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_store_only_: $1: Store Only If Product Exists In Container
Store only if the product item for $1 is already stored in the container. If there is no container in the range that stores product items, items are produced as usual.
translations.@config_automatic_processing_number_of_i: $1: Number Of Items To Stop Charge

When the number of items stored in the container is about to become less than the specified quantity, charge to $1 will be stopped. If set to 0, stopping charge based on the number of items will be disabled.
translations.@config_automatic_feeding_enable_automat: Specify whether to enable the feature for animals to automatically consume feed items from players and containers.
translations.@config_automatic_feeding_feed_search_ra: Specify the range in which the animal searches for food. If set to 0, the default value for each animal will be used. (Unit: meter)
translations.@config_automatic_feeding_need_get_close: Need To Get Close To Eat The Feed
Specify whether the animal needs to approach the container or player to eat the feed.
translations.@config_automatic_feeding_allow_to_feed_: Specify the types of animals allowed to feed from the container.
Specify the types of animals allowed to feed from the player inventory.
translations.@config_automatic_repair_enable_automati: Specify whether to enable the feature that automatically repairs items and pieces.
translations.@config_automatic_repair_crafting_statio: Specify the range to search for a crafting station to be used to repair items. Setting to 0 disables periodic item repair. (Unit: meters)
translations.@config_automatic_repair_repair_items_wh: Repair Items When Accessing The Crafting Station
Specify whether or not to repair all items that can be repaired when a crafting station's GUI is opened.
translations.@config_automatic_repair_item_repair_mes: Specify where the message is displayed when an item is repaired.
translations.@config_automatic_repair_piece_search_ra: Specify the range to search for pieces to repair. Setting to 0 disables periodic piece repair. (Unit: meters)
translations.@config_automatic_repair_piece_repair_me: Specify where the message is displayed when a piece is repaired.
translations.@config_automatic_mining_enable_automati: Specify whether to enable the feature that mines minerals automatically.
translations.@config_automatic_mining_need_to_equip_p: Need To Equip Pickaxe For Mining

Specify whether a pickaxe needs to be equipped to attempt automatic mining. Disabling this option uses the equipped pickaxe if it can mine the target, otherwise the lowest-tier pickaxe in the player's inventory that can. If no suitable pickaxe is found, automatic mining is not attempted.
translations.@config_automatic_mining_mining_interval: Specify the interval between mining attempts. (Unit: seconds)
translations.@config_automatic_mining_mining_range_de: Specify the maximum distance to search for a mineral. If set to 0, the pickaxe's attack range is used. (Unit: meters)
translations.@config_automatic_mining_allow_mining_mi: Specify the minerals to be automatically mined.
translations.@config_automatic_mining_allow_mining_un: Specify whether or not to allow mining underground minerals.
translations.@config_automatic_mining_need_to_equip_w: Need To Equip Wishbone For Mining Underground Minerals
Specify whether or not to require a wishbone to mine underground minerals.
translations.@config_automatic_mining_mining_key_desc: Specify a shortcut key to attempt mining. If a valid shortcut key is assigned to this option, mining at regular intervals is disabled.
translations.@config_automatic_mining_enable_area_min: Specify whether a pickaxe swing that hits an allowed mineral also hits other allowed minerals and rock sections near the hit point. Each extra target wears the pickaxe as a hit does; stamina and skill gain stay once per swing. Requires the module to be running.
translations.@config_automatic_mining_area_mining_rad: Specify how far from the hit point area mining reaches. (Unit: meters)
translations.@config_automatic_mining_area_mining_max: Specify the maximum number of extra minerals or rock sections one swing can hit.
translations.@config_automatic_storage_enable_automat: Specify whether to enable the feature that stores player inventory items into nearby containers when the storage shortcut is pressed.
translations.@config_automatic_storage_storage_search: Specify the maximum distance to search for containers. (Unit: meters)
translations.@config_automatic_storage_container_refe: Specify the maximum number of nearby containers to reference in distance order. Set to 0 for unlimited.
translations.@config_automatic_storage_allow_containe: Specify containers that allow automatic storage. Private chests are excluded by default.
translations.@config_automatic_storage_allowed_item_t: Specify Valheim item types that can be stored automatically.
translations.@config_automatic_storage_excluded_items: Specify items that automatic storage must keep in the player inventory. Plain entries are case-insensitive partial matches against internal names, prefab names, and localized display names. Prefix an entry with r/ to use a regular expression.
translations.@config_automatic_storage_store_hotbar_i: Specify whether items in the hotbar row can be stored automatically.
translations.@config_automatic_storage_store_items_ke: Specify the shortcut key that stores eligible inventory items into nearby containers once. If no key is assigned, automatic storage does not run.
translations.@config_automatic_storage_storage_messag: Specify where the message is displayed after items are stored.
translations.@config_automatic_pickup_automatic_picku: Specify the range within which objects are automatically picked up. (Unit: meters)
Specify the interval at which objects are automatically picked up. Setting it to 0 disables periodic automatic pickup. (Unit: second)
translations.@config_automatic_pickup_pickup_all_near: Interacting with a pickable object using this key picks up all of the same objects within range at once. Periodic automatic pickup keeps running at its interval whether or not this key is assigned.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_enable_automat: Specify whether to enable the feature that harvests grown crops and replants the regrowing sapling at the harvested spot. With the Player Inventory seed source it works around the player; with Nearby Containers it works around the containers you designate.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_farming_interv: Specify the interval between farming attempts. (Unit: seconds)
translations.@config_automatic_farming_farming_range_: Specify the maximum distance to search for crops to harvest. (Unit: meters)
translations.@config_automatic_farming_allow_farming_: Specify the crops to be automatically harvested and replanted. Crops that have no plantable sapling are harvested only.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_seed_reserve_d: Specify the number of each seed item to keep in the active seed source. Planting stops consuming a seed once its count would drop below this value.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_seed_source_de: Specify where planting draws seeds from. Player Inventory keeps the original behavior: crops are searched, harvested, and replanted around you and seeds come from your inventory. Nearby Containers makes farming container-based: the search is anchored to the containers you designate (see Designate Container Role), each planting box draws its input only from same-role boxes within Farming Range, and harvested yield is deposited into storage boxes first, otherwise the matching planting box, never the player inventory. The Seed Reserve is kept within whichever pool is in use.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_enable_proacti: Specify whether to also sow seeds into nearby empty cultivated ground, in addition to replanting harvested spots.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_sowing_spacing: Specify the multiplier applied to each sapling's grow radius to derive the sowing grid spacing. Higher values space saplings farther apart.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_farming_key_de: Specify a shortcut key to attempt farming. If a valid shortcut key is assigned to this option, farming at regular intervals is disabled.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_designate_cont: Specify a shortcut key that cycles the role of the container you are looking at between none, cultivation, seed harvest, and storage. When Seed Source is set to Nearby Containers, a cultivation box grows crops from the seeds it holds, a seed-harvest box grows seeds from the crops it holds, and harvested yield is deposited into nearby storage boxes first, otherwise back into the matching planting box. Changing a role claims ownership of the chest, so it only works on containers you can access.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_enable_grid_pl: Hold the grid planting key while planting by hand to add a grid of the same crop. Each extra crop costs what a hand-placed crop costs: seeds from your inventory (and from nearby containers while Automatic Supply is running), stamina and cultivator durability. As in vanilla, seeds are not needed in free-build worlds. Invalid cells are skipped; planting stops when you cannot pay. Independent of automatic farming, Seed Source and Seed Reserve.
translations.@config_automatic_farming_grid_planting_: Hold this key while placing a crop to plant a grid. While it is held, the crop preview also snaps to the rows of a growing crop of the same kind nearby (same spacing and orientation), so a new grid lines up with an earlier one. An unbound key makes every manual crop placement plant a grid, except while alternate placement (AltPlace) is held. Left Alt does not conflict with vanilla alternate placement.
Number of cells per side, including the manually planted crop. Set to 1 to disable. The grid follows the placement rotation and uses grow radius multiplied by Sowing Spacing Factor for spacing.
translations.@config_automatic_supply_supply_range_de: Specify the range around the player within which containers supply items for manual crafting, building, planting and station intake. Items in the inventory are used first, then containers from the nearest. Containers you cannot access, such as warded, private or in-use ones, are never used. (Unit: meters)
translations.@config_common_disable_module_runtime_de: You can disable this feature completely to avoid adding logic you don't need. This module applies the change while the game is running, so no restart is needed.
translations.@message_automatic_mapping_pin_duplicate: A pin with this name is already nearby.
translations.@message_automatic_farming_container_des: Cannot change this container's farming role
translations.@message_automatic_supply_inventory_full: Inventory full: could not take items from nearby containers
translations.@message_automatic_supply_missing_materi: Could not take the missing materials from nearby containers
translations.@command_common_help_description: Displays a help message and exits the command.
translations.@command_automatics_description: Displays the usage of commands added by Automatics.
translations.@command_automatics_option_include_descr: Show only commands whose names include the word specified in this option.
translations.@command_automatics_option_exclude_descr: Exclude commands whose names contain the word specified with this option.
translations.@command_automatics_option_verbose_descr: Displays detailed usage of the command.
translations.@command_printnames_description: Outputs internal or display names that contain the specified string or match the specified regular expression. If multiple arguments are specified, only those matching all of them will be output.
translations.@command_printnames_extra_option:
WORD:   A text contained in the internal or display name. (e.g. $enemy_, $item_, $piece_, Boar, Mushroom, Wood door); All partially matching internal and display names are output.
REGEXP: A regular expression of the internal or display name to be output. Must be prefixed with r/ (e.g. r/^[$]item_, r/^boar$)
translations.@command_printnames_extra_description:
Examples:
printnames ling r/^[$]enemy_
printnames r/^[$@]location_.+(?<!_(enter|exit))$
printnames mushroom r/^[$]item_.+(?<!_description)$
translations.@command_printobjects_description: Display nearby objects that can be handled by Automatics.
translations.@command_printobjects_extra_option: TYPE: Type of object to be displayed. Specify one of the following: animal, container, door, dungeon, flora, mineral, monster, spawner, spot, vehicle, other.
translations.@command_printobjects_option_radius_desc: Specify the range within which the object is to be searched. [Default: 32] (Unit: meters)
translations.@command_printobjects_option_number_desc: Specify how many objects matching the condition are to be displayed. [Default: 4]
translations.@command_printobjects_option_include_des: Show only objects whose internal or display names match the word specified in this option. It works as a regular expression by concatenating r/ at the beginning of the string. Not applied to the dungeon and spot types.
translations.@command_printobjects_option_exclude_des: Exclude objects whose internal names or display names match the word specified with this option. It works as a regular expression by concatenating r/ at the beginning of the string. Not applied to the dungeon and spot types.
translations.@command_printobjects_extra_description: Note: The result of this command may show objects that you feel are not of the target type. For example, Flint may appear in a Flora search. This is not a bug but means that Automatics can treat Flint as Flora.
translations.@command_printobjects_message_result_mor: In addition to this, found $1 types of objects that can be treated as $2.
translations.@command_printobjects_message_result_emp: No $1 matching the criteria were found.
translations.@command_printobjects_message_mapping_no: Automatic Mapping is not running: fish, birds and ships are missing from this list, and nothing listed is pinned. This command does not turn Automatic Mapping on.
translations.@command_printobjects_error_player_unava: The local player is not available yet.
translations.@command_printobjects_error_world_unavai: The world location data is not available yet.
translations.@command_removemappins_description: Remove the map pins that match the specified conditions. By default, it runs in safe mode and only removes duplicate pins. [Caution] To prevent accidental actions, please temporarily disable the 'Automatic Mapping' when using this command.
translations.@command_removemappins_option_radius_des: Specify the maximum distance from the player's position to the pin to be removed. If set to 0, all pins will be targeted. [Default: 0] (Unit: meters)
translations.@command_removemappins_option_include_de: Pins that contain the specified string in their name will be targeted for deletion.
translations.@command_removemappins_option_exclude_de: Pins that contain the specified string in their name will be excluded from the deletion target.
translations.@command_removemappins_option_dry_run_de: Enables the dry run mode. When this option is specified, pin deletion will be skipped, and only text output to the console will be performed.
translations.@command_removemappins_option_dangerous_: When this option is specified, non-duplicate pins will also be included in the deletion target. Please use this option with caution, as incorrect usage can result in the deletion of all pins on the map.
translations.@command_removemappins_message_safe_mode: The removemappins command ran in safe mode, so only duplicate pins (pins at the same position as another pin) were targeted. To also remove pins that are not duplicates, enable the "dangerous-mode" option. For more details, run "removemappins -h" to see the help.
